headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks; data leakage and compliance are limited by the profiles, while capability conflict is low due to no overlapping writes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata can ingest content through APIs, events, webhooks, and an MCP server, while Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks. That creates a plausible path for attacker-controlled content from one agent to be treated as instructions by the other in default integrations. The pairwise interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests Plane-originated webhook, event, or file content without provenance checks
IF Plane forwards OpenMetadata-generated text into task descriptions or notes that are later parsed as instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic parsing of cross-agent content
Add provenance labels to all imported records
Restrict MCP/webhook handlers to allowlisted schemas
Require manual review before copying outputs between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge data, while Plane touches issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, images, hyperlinks, and notes. Plane has broad network egress but no filesystem write, so the main leakage path is shared content moving between systems rather than uncontrolled exfiltration. The profiles do not show a shared workspace or secrets handling, so blast radius appears limited.
conditions: IF sensitive governance or lineage data from OpenMetadata is copied into Plane issues or file uploads
IF Plane network egress is used to transmit imported content to external services
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive metadata in Plane tickets
Redact identifiers before file upload
Turn off external integrations on Plane
Use separate workspaces for sensitive catalogs and task tracking

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and uses APIs/SDKs/events/webhooks/MCP, while Plane supports multiple instances but lacks filesystem write. Because only one agent can write filesystems and no shared mutable write surface is documented, direct write-write conflict is not evident. Uncertainty remains about API-level contention, so the lower severity is chosen but not none.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to mutate the same external API-backed resource
IF an orchestrator routes both agents to the same mutable record without locking
mitigations: Assign separate resource namespaces
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Disable concurrent edits on shared records
Use optimistic-locking or version checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata can generate governance and lineage outputs that Plane can plausibly ingest as issues, notes, or hyperlinks. If Plane treats those outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into tasking or scheduling decisions. The profiles do not show verification gates between them, so the interaction is plausible in default integrations but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Plane imports OpenMetadata outputs into tasks or notes without human verification
IF downstream users act on those imported records as authoritative
mitigations: Require human approval before creating tasks from catalog output
Add a verification step for imported facts
Mark imported content as untrusted by default
Limit automation to non-actionable summaries

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata explicitly touches governance and lineage data, while Plane handles issues, files, notes, and roadmaps. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, so a concrete compliance breach cannot be established. The risk is limited to policy mismatch if regulated data is copied into Plane.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Plane without matching retention or residency controls
IF OpenMetadata governance records are exported into Plane for broader access
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Plane
Apply retention labels before export
Review residency requirements for each workspace
Use separate access-controlled projects
